title: Month close
description: Optional operational close for a calendar month. This is not statutory accounting — it freezes operational history so corrections stay explicit.

moduleOff.title: Month close is off
moduleOff.body: Turn on Month close under Settings → Features, or open a period once to enable it automatically.

notAllowed: You need month-close access to view this page.

periods.title: Periods
periods.empty: No periods yet. Open a month to begin.

detail.select: Select a period to review completeness.

closed.notice: This month is closed. Silent rewrites are blocked — record an explicit adjustment or economic correction. Original records stay unchanged.

completeness.empty: Completeness has not been computed yet.
completeness.issueCount: {count, plural, one {# open item} other {# open items}}

adjustments.title: Post-close adjustment
adjustments.hint: Explain why operational history needs an explicit correction, supersede, or adjustment after close.
adjustments.economicHint: Amount is optional. Leave it empty for an audit-only note. When filled, this row folds into project Actual (cost) or invoiced (revenue) once through the financial compose engine — original expenses and bills are never rewritten.
adjustments.supersedeHint: The original row stays on the ledger but is excluded from totals. This amount replaces it in compose.
adjustments.explainability: Closed-month history is immutable. Amounts shown here are the correction rows themselves — project Actual and billing totals come from compose only, never a second engine on this page.

errors.invalidTransition: That status change is not allowed.
errors.monthClosed: This month is closed. Open Month close and record an explicit post-close adjustment instead of changing the original record.
errors.notClosed: Post-close adjustments require a closed month.
errors.currencyMismatch: Economic corrections must use the organization base currency.
errors.supersedeWrongPeriod: You can only supersede a correction in the same closed month.
errors.supersedeNotEconomic: You can only supersede an economic correction that has an amount.
errors.alreadySuperseded: That correction is already superseded. Supersede the current row instead.
errors.supersedeWrongProject: You can only supersede a correction on the same project.
errors.supersedeWrongSide: You can only supersede a correction on the same economic side.
errors.supersedeWrongCurrency: You can only supersede a correction in the same currency.
